title: Tensor, internal Hom and diagram calculus of enriched infinity categories
statement:
Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. Spaces, enriched object spaces and indexing simplicial sets are $\mathcal U$-small; categories of such objects are formed in $\mathcal U'$, and presentability and small (co)limits are relative to $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably symmetric monoidal infinity category: it admits all small limits and colimits, is generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a small collection of presentable objects, and its tensor preserves small colimits separately. A $\mathcal V$-category has objects, mapping objects in $\mathcal V$, and associative unital composition with coherent homotopies; equivalences of such categories mean fully faithful and essentially surjective enriched functors. Write $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ for their infinity category. It is presentable, has all small limits and colimits, and is closed symmetric monoidal. Its tensor has objects $(a,b)$ and mapping objects $\mathcal A(a,a')\otimes\mathcal B(b,b')$, with completion understood; its internal Hom is the enriched category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ of coherent enriched functors and transformations. There are natural coherent equivalences
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal B,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal B,\mathcal E)).$$
The tensor preserves small colimits separately. Limits of full enriched subcategory inclusions are full inclusions, whose objects satisfy the corresponding inverse-image conditions.

For a small infinity category $K$, free enrichment $K_{\mathcal V}$ is left adjoint to the underlying-category functor $U$, where $U\mathcal E$ has mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf1,\mathcal E(x,y))$. Free enrichment is induced by $S\mapsto S\otimes\mathbf1=\operatorname{colim}_{S}\mathbf1$ from spaces. The enriched category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(K_{\mathcal V},\mathcal E)$ is the cotensor $\mathcal E^K$: its objects are coherent diagrams $K\to U\mathcal E$ and its mapping objects retain coherent natural transformations. These cotensors exist also for small simplicial diagram shapes, by their freely generated infinity categories, and satisfy
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\mathcal E^K)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal A,\mathcal E)^K.$$
In an enriched functor category or a cotensor, a transformation is an equivalence if and only if every object component is an equivalence. Composition, evaluation, currying and cotensor identifications are coherent. Opposite categories are defined by reversing the mapping objects and using symmetry in composition; they give an involutive equivalence on $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$.

These assertions apply to $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, the enhanced localization of unbounded cochain complexes of abelian groups at quasi-isomorphisms, with derived tensor and unit $\mathbf Z[0]$; the cochain and quasi-isomorphism conventions are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here mapping-object equivalence means equivalence of complexes in the enhanced derived category, not just equality of degree-zero cohomology.

For precision, the operadic presentation of these notions is [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; all smallness and presentability assertions are relative to the fixed smaller universe, with the categories of such objects formed in the larger universe.

source.place: Haugseng, On the tensor product of enriched infinity-categories, Corollaries 9.3-9.4, Remark 9.5 and Corollary 10.8; Gepner-Haugseng, Enriched infinity-categories via nonsymmetric infinity-operads, sections 4.3, 5.5 and Proposition 5.7.8, with base change Proposition 5.7.17. The later paper repairs the old colimit argument. The cotensor, componentwise-equivalence, limit and D(Z) specializations are part of this generic structural foundation. Read online; not archived. No Stacks tag supplies it.

external.place: Sections 4.3 and 5.5, Proposition 5.7.8 and Proposition 5.7.17; presentability, coherent functors, and change-of-enrichment adjunction.

proof.text: Present the enrichment by algebroids as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. By [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability], $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ is presentable. By [lem-coef-algebroid-completion], completeness is locality for the single map $s:E^1\to E^0$. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] with the small set $\{s\}$. This produces the reflector $L$, makes the complete-object category presentable, computes its limits in algebroids and its colimits as $L\operatorname{colim}_{\operatorname{Algd}}$. The same completion theorem identifies its equivalences with fully faithful essentially surjective functors. These are exactly the category and equivalences of the statement; no ordinary homotopy-category localization is substituted.

Form the external product of [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product] and apply the monoidal multiplication $\mu:\mathcal V\times\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$. Before completion its objects are pairs and its Hom object is $A(a,a')\otimes B(b,b')$. Its composition first interchanges the middle factors by symmetry and then applies the two given compositions. The external-product theorem supplies the coherent symmetric monoidal structure, not just its binary operation. By [lem-coef-algebroid-completion] it respects completion equivalences, so this structure descends with tensor $L(A\otimes B)$ and completed unit $L\mathbf1$. The unit is completed when necessary; the assertion about pairs is a presentation, and is not a claim that completion preserves the object space.

Apply [lem-coef-algebroid-bilinear-colimits] with $b=\mu$ and $\mathcal W=\mathcal T=\mathcal V$; symmetry makes $\mu$ strong monoidal, and its separate cocontinuity is the hypothesis on $\mathcal V$. For a small diagram $(A_i)$ and a complete $B$, put $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{\operatorname{Algd}}A_i$. Completion compatibility gives $L(LQ\otimes B)\simeq L(Q\otimes B)$, since $Q\to LQ$ is a completion equivalence. The latter is $L\operatorname{colim}_i(A_i\otimes B)$ by bilinear cocontinuity, and hence $\operatorname{colim}_{\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V},i}L(A_i\otimes B)$. This proves separate cocontinuity, including the empty diagram. For a complete $A$ and a diagram $(B_i)$, put $P=\operatorname{colim}_{\operatorname{Algd}}B_i$. In the other variable the comparisons are $L(A\otimes LP)\simeq L(A\otimes P)\simeq L\operatorname{colim}_i(A\otimes B_i)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V},i}L(A\otimes B_i)$: the first uses completion compatibility on $P\to LP$, the second bilinear cocontinuity in its second variable, and the third the reflector colimit formula. This uses Haugseng's repaired theorem, not the incorrect old inference that a separately cocontinuous multiplication preserves all colimits of the product category.

source.place: Corollary 9.2, then the completion argument of Corollary 9.3; introduction identifies the old gap

proof.text: Since $-\otimes A$ preserves colimits on the presentable category obtained in step 1, [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] gives its right adjoint $[A,-]$. Its counit is evaluation $[A,E]\otimes A\to E$. Maps from the unit to $[A,E]$ are enriched functors $A\to E$. More precisely, use the free two-object $v$-edge test of [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability], fixing its endpoints to functors $F,G$. Maps from this test to $[A,E]$ are maps from its tensor with $A$ to $E$. Such a map is precisely a family $v\otimes A(a,b)\to E(Fa,Gb)$ compatible with all composition and identity operations. Thus the mapping object of $[A,E]$ represents coherent $v$-parametrized enriched transformations. This identifies $[A,E]$ with $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(A,E)$, retaining the whole mapping object. Completion of probes does not change their maps into a complete target. Composition of transformations comes from the composite of two evaluations; its identities and higher associativity come from the monoidal associativity already constructed and the adjunction identities.

source.place: Remark 9.5; identifying the adjoint by the free-graph test of Gepner-Haugseng Remark 4.3.4

proof.text: Construct currying by taking the adjoint of $[A,[B,E]]\otimes A\otimes B\to[B,E]\otimes B\to E$. Equivalently a functor out of $C\otimes A\otimes B$ is adjointed first across $B$ and then across $A$. The two inverse uncurrying operations are evaluation, so the unit/counit triangle identities give inverse maps between $[A\otimes B,E]$ and $[A,[B,E]]$. Testing with every free $v$-edge of [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability] gives the same inverse on mapping objects and transformation homotopies. Thus this is the asserted enriched equivalence, not only a bijection on functor classes. Repeated currying and evaluation agree because they are adjuncts of the same iterated evaluation map; their specified coherence is inherited from the coherent adjunctions of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints].

source.place: Remark 9.5; formal tensor-Hom calculus after the repaired colimit theorem

proof.text: For a small coherent diagram of full subcategory inclusions $A_j\hookrightarrow B_j$, [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability] computes the two limits on object spaces and mapping objects; [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] and the locality description in [lem-coef-algebroid-completion] compute the same limits inside complete objects. A compatible object $b=(b_j)$ of $\lim B_j$ lies in the image precisely when each $b_j$ belongs to $A_j$: full subcategories include every arrow and coherence among their objects, so the compatibility data then already lie in the $A_j$. For two such objects the map on Hom objects is the limit of the equivalences $A_j(a_j,a'_j)\simeq B_j(a_j,a'_j)$, hence an equivalence. Therefore the limit is a full inclusion with exactly the stated inverse-image conditions. For an empty diagram it is the identity of the terminal enriched category.

source.place: Section 4.3, graphwise limits; section 5.4, locality is closed under limits

proof.text: For a space $S$, put $t(S)=\operatorname{colim}_S\mathbf1$. The colimit universal property gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(t(S),v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Spc}}(S,\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf1,v))$. Moreover separate preservation of colimits computes $t(S)\otimes t(T)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{S\times T}(\mathbf1\otimes\mathbf1)\simeq t(S\times T)$ and $t(*)\simeq\mathbf1$; all iterated comparisons are the ones induced by these same colimit cocones. Apply [lem-coef-enrichment-change-adjunction] to this strong monoidal colimit-preserving $t$ and its lax monoidal right adjoint. Its spaces-enriched source is ordinary infinity categories by the complete Segal-space identification in that lemma. Consequently $K_{\mathcal V}=Lt_*K$ is left adjoint to $U$, and $UE$ has exactly the mapping spaces asserted in the item.

Define $E^K=[K_{\mathcal V},E]$. For every standard simplex category $[n]$, the strong monoidality of $t$ and the explicit external product give $([n]\times K)_{\mathcal V}\simeq[n]_{\mathcal V}\otimes K_{\mathcal V}$. Before completion the comparison has object space $\{0,\ldots,n\}\times\operatorname{Ob}(K)$, and on each mapping object it is the strong-monoidal comparison $t(S\times T)\simeq t(S)\otimes t(T)$. The operadic compositions are the same colimit-induced operations of step 7. Completing this comparison and using completion compatibility on either factor gives the displayed equivalence. Applying the adjunction of step 7 and then the tensor-Hom adjunction identifies $n$-simplices of the complete Segal nerve of $U[E^K]$ with coherent functors $[n]\times K\to UE$, naturally in all face and degeneracy maps. Thus $U(E^K)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,UE)$, including its arrows and higher homotopies; in degree zero its objects are precisely coherent $K$-diagrams. Its enriched mapping objects are still those computed by the $v$-edge test in step 4, rather than the spaces obtained after $U$. This is the stated enriched cotensor.

source.place: Sections 4.3 and 5.4, change of enrichment and complete Segal-space interpretation; tensor-Hom in Haugseng Remark 9.5

proof.text: The cotensor comparison is the composite $[A,[K_{\mathcal V},E]]\simeq[A\otimes K_{\mathcal V},E]\simeq[K_{\mathcal V},[A,E]]$, using symmetry for the middle interchange. Its maps are iterated evaluations as in step 5. This proves $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(A,E^K)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(A,E)^K$, with coherent composition, not just an equivalence on objects. For a small simplicial shape $K$, take $K^{\mathrm{cat}}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-shape-categorification] and use $E^{K^{\mathrm{cat}}}$. That lemma identifies all the resulting underlying diagram categories with the prescribed simplicial diagrams, including transformations. Smallness stays in the same indexing universe.

source.place: Remark 9.5, formal currying; HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1 for arbitrary simplicial shapes

proof.text: Let $\alpha:F\Rightarrow G$ be an enriched transformation in $[A,E]$. Evaluation shows that an equivalence has equivalence components. Conversely suppose each $\alpha_a$ is an equivalence. Let $J$ be the nerve of the groupoid with two objects and exactly one arrow between any ordered pair. The chosen-edge inclusion $q:\Delta^1\hookrightarrow J$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, since both realizations are contractible, and $J$ is Kan. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] with this $q$: restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ on equivalence arrows, for any infinity category $C$. On cores this is an equivalence of spaces, hence its homotopy fiber over any equivalence is contractible. Applying the same equivalence to space-parametrized families gives coherent inverses $\beta_a$ and their unit/counit homotopies over the object space, including higher coherence data. The enriched naturality homotopy for each mapping object is $G_{a,b}(-)\alpha_a\simeq\alpha_bF_{a,b}(-)$. Precompose with $\beta_a$ and postcompose with $\beta_b$, and use the two inverse homotopies to obtain $\beta_bG_{a,b}(-)\simeq F_{a,b}(-)\beta_a$. To see that the inverse is enriched, composition with $\alpha_a$ on any $E(x,Fa)$ has inverse composition with $\beta_a$; the two composites are homotopic to the identity by the chosen inverse homotopies. Applying $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(v,-)$ for every $v$ makes these inverse maps of spaces. Thus every naturality simplex with parameter $v$ is sent by pre- and postcomposition to the displayed inverse-naturality simplex, and a composition simplex is sent to its composition simplex by associativity in $E$. Faces and degeneracies commute with these maps of spaces. The equivalence of functor categories just obtained supplies their unit/counit homotopies coherently over the object space. These data therefore define a coherent enriched transformation $\beta$. The same transported unit/counit simplices give $\beta\alpha\simeq1$ and $\alpha\beta\simeq1$ as enriched transformations. Hence $\alpha$ is an equivalence. Apply this with $A=K_{\mathcal V}$ for cotensors.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.1.21 (Tag 01MY), with Proposition 6.3.1.13 (Tag 01MS) and Definition 6.3.1.9 (Tag 01MP), specialized to the chosen edge of the walking isomorphism; HTT sections 1.2.4-1.2.7 for inverse transport.

proof.text: Reverse an algebroid by reversing every string $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ to $(x_n,\ldots,x_0)$ in its many-object associative operad and using the symmetry of $\mathcal V$ to reverse the tensor factors in each operation. Thus $A^{\mathrm{op}}(x,y)=A(y,x)$ and composition is the old composition after interchanging the two factors. The symmetric operadic coherences ensure that all the reversed operations have the required compatible faces and degeneracies. Reversing twice is coherently the identity. Reversal interchanges the objects of $E^1$ and preserves the collapse to $E^0$, so preserves complete objects by [lem-coef-algebroid-completion]. On enriched functors it reverses all mapping maps and leaves the object assignment fixed. It therefore induces the claimed involutive equivalence on $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$.

source.place: Operadic definitions in sections 3.1 and 4.3; direct reversal of strings

proof.text: For the final specialization apply [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] with $R=\mathbf Z$. Its cofibrant unit is $\mathbf Z[0]$, weak equivalences are exactly the quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and it satisfies the pushout-product axiom without a boundedness restriction. By [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], its homotopy coherent localization is presentable symmetric monoidal and its derived tensor preserves small colimits separately. It is the enhanced $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ in the item, so all preceding steps apply. Mapping objects are objects of this localization: equivalence is quasi-isomorphism, detected by all cohomology groups, not by $H^0$ alone. This argument uses projective complexes, not the sheaf flat-model theorem, whose current proof dependency chain already passes through this item.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.4.22 and section 4.1.7, applied to the unbounded projective chain model
